About this role 

The Electrical Assistant Supervisor supports the Electrical Maintenance Supervisor in directing daily electrical maintenance at a mission-critical data center. This role leads and mentors Tier 1–3 technicians, performs hands-on maintenance and troubleshooting of critical power systems such as generators, UPS, switchgear, transformers, and PDUs, and serves as the first point of escalation for complex issues. The Assistant Supervisor enforces LOTO, arc flash, and NFPA 70E and NFPA 70B safety standards, oversees contractors, maintains CMMS records, responds to power alarms and emergencies, and directs shift operations when the primary supervisor is offsite.

What you’ll be doing 

  • Assign daily work, review shift schedules, and prioritize open work orders for the electrical team. Run shift operations when the primary supervisor is offsite.
  • Perform maintenance, inspections, and troubleshooting on critical power systems, including backup generators, UPS systems, switchgear, transformers, and PDUs.
  • Review methods of procedure (MOPs) and safety checklists before work begins. Confirm switching steps are clear, risks are identified, and backup power paths are verified.
  • Lead daily pre-job safety briefings. Enforce LOTO protocols and NFPA 70E standards, and make sure the crew consistently wears proper arc-flash protection and PPE.
  • Escort and monitor outside contractors and vendors performing specialized service or testing. Verify their work meets quality standards and facility rules.
  • Keep accurate records of completed tasks, equipment run hours, and spare parts in the CMMS. Make sure inspection logs and test reports are properly filed.
  • Train and mentor junior technicians on maintenance tasks, diagnostic tools, and safe work habits through consistent day-to-day coaching.
  • Respond immediately to power alarms and system interruptions during shifts and on-call rotations. Assist with emergency recovery to protect the critical data center load.
  • Other duties may be assigned.

What you’ll have 

  • Completion of an electrical apprenticeship, an associate degree in an electrical trade, or equivalent practical experience.
  • At least 4 years of commercial or industrial electrical maintenance experience, including at least 1 year serving as a lead technician or crew chief.
  • Solid understanding of electrical power distribution equipment, including switchgear, generators, transfer switches, and UPS systems.
  • Demonstrated ability to read and interpret electrical one-line diagrams, schematics, and technical manuals.
  • Strong practical knowledge of electrical safety rules, arc-flash hazards, and lockout/tagout procedures.
  • Clear communication skills and the ability to coordinate tasks smoothly across maintenance and operations teams.

Physical requirements and work environment 

  • Ability to stand, walk, and perform repetitive tasks for extended periods 
  • Ability to lift and move equipment as needed (50 pounds) 
  • Ability to work onsite in a mining or data center environment (heat, noise, etc.) 
  • Exposure to high noise levels and varying temperatures 

Safety Requirements 

  • PPE & Compliance: Strictly adhere to all site safety protocols and wear required Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) at all times (e.g., safety glasses, hearing protection, steel-toed boots). 
  • Hazard Awareness: Proactively identify, report, and mitigate potential workplace hazards or unsafe conditions. 
  • Standards: Maintain compliance with OSHA regulations and internal safety training. 
  • Organization: Keep all work areas clean and free of obstructions to prevent workplace accidents. 

Compensation and Benefits  

  • Salary commensurate with experience.  
  • 401(k) retirement plan: Incudes a generous company match. 
  • Comprehensive health coverage: Multiple medical plan options, including 100% company-paid plans, HAS & FSA. 
  • Work-life balance: Paid time off, sick time and floating holidays. 
  • Wellness & lifestyle perks: Enjoy free gym memberships, pet insurance, childcare discounts, employee assistance program, and more to support your life both in and out of work. 

Riot is an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees.

Position Overview
Blockdaemon is looking for a hands-on Site Reliability Engineer to join our Security team and take ownership of the cloud infrastructure that our security posture depends on. This is fundamentally an infrastructure and networking role: you'll be the engineer who designs, hardens, and operates the multi cloud foundation (AWS, GCP, Azure) that everything else sits on top of, with a specific focus on network security, egress control, and infrastructure as code.

You'll work across our full cloud footprint, building and maintaining the Terraform and Ansible that define our environments, running production Kubernetes (GKE), and owning the network layer, including Cloudflare, Tailscale, and egress proxy infrastructure that controls how traffic moves in and out of our systems.

You'll have direct influence over how our cloud environments are structured, secured, and automated, and your work will have a visible, immediate impact on our risk posture and operational resilience.

Your Impact

  • Own the design, reliability, and hardening of multi cloud infrastructure across AWS, GCP, and Azure

  • Build and maintain infrastructure as code (Terraform, Ansible, Helm) as the source of truth for how environments are provisioned and configured

  • Own network security architecture: egress proxy configuration, traffic segmentation, and outbound control across cloud environments

  • Manage and evolve our Cloudflare footprint (DNS, WAF, edge security, traffic routing) and API gateway layer (Zuplo)

  • Operate and secure Tailscale as our zero trust network access layer, including access policy design and rollout to new environments

  • Run production Kubernetes (GKE) with an infrastructure security lens: cluster hardening, network policy, and secure deployment patterns

  • Build observability (Grafana) for network and infrastructure health, so misconfigurations and anomalies are caught before they become incidents

  • Harden CI/CD and deployment pipelines (GitHub, GitLab, ArgoCD) from an infrastructure and supply chain security perspective

  • Manage on-call rotation and incident response for infrastructure and network layer issues, driving root cause analysis and durable fixes rather than one-off patches

  • Reduce toil: identify manual infrastructure work and automate it.

  • Act as the technical bridge between security and platform engineering on anything network or cloud infrastructure related

Role Requirement

  • 5+ years in an SRE, infrastructure, or platform engineering role, with hands-on experience running production workloads across multiple cloud providers — this is not an entry point into SRE

  • Proven experience with SRE fundamentals: defining SLOs, measuring toil, running blameless postmortems, and using reliability data to inform engineering priorities

  • Strong, demonstrable experience with AWS, GCP, and Azure, including their networking primitives (VPCs, peering, firewall rules, load balancing)

  • Proficiency with IaC and configuration management — Terraform and Ansible are both in daily use here and you'll be owning them, not just contributing to them

  • Solid network security background, including experience designing or operating egress control and proxy architecture for security and compliance purposes

  • Hands-on Kubernetes experience in production (we run GKE), including Helm and GitOps deployment patterns (we use ArgoCD)

  • Experience with Cloudflare or a comparable edge/CDN/WAF platform, and familiarity with API gateway technologies

  • Practical experience with Tailscale or another zero trust network access solution

  • Genuine on-call experience: you've carried a pager, driven postmortems, and understand the difference between suppressing an alert and fixing the underlying problem

  • Strong scripting and automation ability in Go or Python — you'll be writing tooling, runbooks, and automation scripts, not one-off fixes

  • Clear communicator who can work directly with security, compliance, and engineering stakeholders without a translation layer

Nice-to-Have Skills

  • Experience with Kafka or other streaming infrastructure, particularly for log and telemetry pipelines

  • Experience supporting a SOC 2 or similar compliance program, ideally with Vanta or a comparable GRC platform

  • Background in fintech, crypto, or another regulated industry where audit readiness and network controls are a constant, not a quarterly event

  • Experience with Temporal or similar workflow orchestration for building reliable automation

  • Exposure to secrets management (HashiCorp Vault) in a multi-cloud context
